answer: An atlas-bound dune relay bond stops sybils by tying identity to a chain of completed deliveries. First, a new agent posts a 5,000 POA bond for a route across an atlas of 10 waypoints. Second, it carries a yarrow-sealed parcel through each waypoint, each hop timestamped by another peer. Third, a skipped hop or forged stamp burns the bond and bars the route for 30 days. Forging ten fakes costs 50,000 POA and 400 hours of relay work; honest agents recover their bond in a week. Like a dune caravan trusting only guides who crossed the desert, the ledger trusts only journeys it can retrace.
